subject: Discovery recap: MediCore decision criteria + bakeoff probes
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@medicore.ai>
Cc: Tomás Ruiz <tomas.ruiz@medicore.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: MediCore decision criteria + bakeoff probes

Hi Alyssa / Tomás — thanks again for the intro call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we kick off the bakeoff.

High-level takeaways (your goals):
- Latency SLO: P99 < 400ms for 2k reqs/min (model: code‑assist + domain prompts)
- Cost target: < $0.015 per 1k tokens over steady‑state usage (90% of traffic)
- Data controls: VPC + customer‑managed KMS required, logs retained 1 year, auditability for model inputs/outputs
- Quality: top‑of‑stack accuracy on entity extraction and hallucination rate under 1.5% for the test set you gave

Key risks you highlighted:
- Concurrent capacity during month‑end reporting windows
- Need for deterministic behavior for compliance sampling
- Integrations with your preprocessing lambda (Python 3.11)

Competitive context you shared:
- Running an internal PoC with Vendor X (already in prod for one model family)
- Evaluating Vendor Y for lower cost but unclear on VPC/KMS story

Proposed bakeoff plan (attached: bakeoff-test-plan.csv) — short version:
1) Functional checks: prompt parity, hallucination probes (two days)
2) Performance sweep: 3 ramp profiles incl. month‑end burst (48 hours)
3) Cost run: steady‑state sampling and token accounting (24 hours)
4) Security check: VPC/KMS proof and ingest path validation (ASAP)

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Alyssa: confirm which internal test corpus you want us to use (the sample S3 path you mentioned vs. the redacted CSV).
- Tomás: can you confirm the procurement timeline (PO vs contract signature) and target decision date?
- Marissa / Karthik (cc): we’ll need a quick vendor matrix for the exec readout after the run — can you draft with the decision criteria columns (SLO, cost/op, security, integrations, ops maturity)?

Attachments: bakeoff-test-plan.csv (test cases + ramp profiles)

If that looks good I’ll schedule the perf window for next Tuesday/Wednesday and share access instructions for the VPC proof.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
T: +1 415‑555‑0123

From: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@medicore.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Tomás Ruiz <tomas.ruiz@medicore.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: MediCore decision criteria + bakeoff probes

Thanks Tessa — this is very helpful and captures the call. A few clarifications: 

1) Test corpus: use s3://medicore‑tests/2027/q2/redacted_prompts.csv — that’s the clean set. We’ll also provide a separate set with edge cases (PII redacted).
2) Decision date: aiming for July 12 board readout, procurement needs a signed SOW by July 5 to hit that.
3) Security: we need to validate KMS key rotation and HSM integration (if available) — if you can include a short checklist that’d speed approvals.

Also: Vendor X has already committed to a one‑week parallel load test; happy to run both in the same windows but we’d prefer staggered start times to avoid noisy overlap.

Tomás — I’ll coordinate the SOW draft with procurement once we agree on the test plan.

—Alyssa
Alyssa Park
Product Lead, AI Integrations
MediCore Analytics

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@medicore.ai>
Cc: Tomás Ruiz <tomas.ruiz@medicore.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: MediCore decision criteria + bakeoff probes

Perfect — thanks for the timelines and the S3 path. Two operational notes:

1) Stagger plan: propose Redwood start 06/29 00:00 UTC, Vendor X start 06/30 08:00 UTC. That gives ~32 hours separation. Does that work for you?
2) KMS/HSM checklist: attaching a short SLA + checklist (MediCore_SLA_draft.pdf) — includes rotation, audit log requirements, and ops contacts.

Marissa / Karthik — can you do the vendor matrix and a quick health check runbook by EOD tomorrow? Specific asks for the matrix:
- Column A: Decision criteria (SLO, cost, security, integration effort, operational maturity)
- Column B/C/D: Redwood / Vendor X / Vendor Y live evidence (links or short notes)
- Highlight any blind spots we need to probe during perf window

Alyssa / Tomás — I’ll also share temporary VPC access steps (read‑only test subnet) once you confirm the start date.

Attaching: MediCore_SLA_draft.pdf; bakeoff-test-plan.csv

Tessa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@medicore.ai>, Tomás Ruiz <tomas.ruiz@medicore.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Draft vendor matrix + quick runbook (for Tessa review)

Attached is a short vendor matrix snapshot (3 rows) and a two‑page runbook for the perf windows. Key flags I added: 
- Vendor X: proven latency in prior tests but no explicit customer KMS integration; requires separate network steps.
- Vendor Y: good cost profile, limited observability and missing token‑level tracing which could be a gating item for you.
- Redwood: VPC + KMS support is available now; we propose a canary traffic route + fallback to lower‑cost variant to protect SLAs.

Runbook highlights (short):
- Pre‑run: verify test keys + rotate KMS key in staging; smoke test prompts (30 min)
- Ramp: linear 0→100% over 1 hour, sustained 4 hours, spike window 30 min at 4x baseline
- Data collection: token counts, per‑token cost, P99 latency, failure traces, hallucination counterexamples
- Post‑run: artifact zip (logs + sample outputs) and exec summary template

I’ll iterate on the matrix after we have the perf results. Karthik — can you add a short note about the integration effort (approx. dev days) by EOD?

Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attached: vendor_matrix_snapshot.xlsx (stub), perf_runbook_v1.pdf (stub)

From: Tomás Ruiz <tomas.ruiz@medicore.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@medicore.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: MediCore decision criteria + bakeoff probes

Sounds good to me — confirm the 06/29 start for Redwood and please send the SOW draft (Tomás.PRuiz@medicore.ai for procurement). Let’s aim to keep the window non‑overlapping with Vendor X as proposed.

Thanks,
Tomás
CTO, MediCore Analytics
